# shopify_checkout_and_accounts_configuration (Resource)

The branding of a checkout and accounts configuration: colours, corner radii, typography and component styles of checkout and customer accounts. **A poor fit for Terraform:** branding is usually edited in the admin's checkout editor, and every edit there to a managed value shows as drift. Configurations are created and published in the checkout editor; the API can't create, delete or publish them, so this resource adopts an existing one and destroy only removes it from state, leaving the branding as it is. If another configuration is published later, the resource keeps following its own one (`is_published` turns `false`); import again to follow the new one. Overrides are not managed. Import with `published` or the configuration name.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Name unset: the published configuration. Only the keys written here are managed.
resource "shopify_checkout_and_accounts_configuration" "live" {
  branding = jsonencode({
    designTokens = {
      colors       = { palette = { color1 = "#1A4D8F" } }
      cornerRadius = { base = 6 }
    }
    components = {
      checkbox = { cornerRadius = "LARGE" }
      # null resets this value to Shopify's default.
      primaryButton = null
    }
  })
}

# Destroy only removes the configuration from state; the branding stays.
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `branding` (String) Branding as a JSON object in the API's camelCase, following [`CheckoutAndAccountsConfigurationBrandingInput`](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin-graphql/2026-10/input-objects/CheckoutAndAccountsConfigurationBrandingInput); write it with `jsonencode()`. Only the keys you write are managed: a missing key is left alone, and `null` resets that value (or a whole subtree) to Shopify's default. Removing a key from the config stops managing it but keeps its value in Shopify; set it to `null` and apply first to reset it. Unset means branding is not managed. Colours compare case-insensitively and numbers numerically, and edits in the admin to keys you didn't write never show as drift. **Write-only, never checked for drift:** images (`components.favicon`, `components.header.logo.image`, `surfaces.{checkout,customerAccounts,signIn}.components.header.logo.image`, `surfaces.checkout.components.header.cartLink.image`, `surfaces.checkout.components.orderSummary.backgroundImage`, `surfaces.signIn.components.main.backgroundImage`), fonts (`designTokens.typography.primary`, `designTokens.typography.secondary`) and `components.merchandiseThumbnail.aspectRatio`. Import and `terraform query` leave them out. Shopify checks keys and values; an invalid value rejects the whole update.
- `name` (String) Name of the configuration to manage, as shown in the checkout editor. Unset means the published configuration. Names come from the shop name, so leaving it unset is what works on every store. Changing it manages a different configuration; the old one keeps its branding.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Configuration GID.
- `is_published` (Boolean) Whether the configuration is the one live on checkout.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# published, or the configuration name; import brings in the whole live branding
terraform import shopify_checkout_and_accounts_configuration.live published
```
